key_insight: A geometrically exact planar beam formulation can incorporate hyperelasticity cleanly when cross-sectional kinematics and out-of-plane constitutive assumptions are treated separately.
engineering_relevance: This gives engineers a more consistent beam model for large-deformation problems where Poisson coupling and thickness stretch can affect predicted stiffness and local response.
method: Start from a conventional three-field geometrically exact planar beam model.
Add a global in-plane thickness deformation field to enrich the kinematics.
Use separate plane-stress or plane-strain constitutive reductions for the out-of-plane direction, with Saint Venant-Kirchhoff and Neo-Hookean material laws.
evidence_signal: Benchmark results in the abstract show plane stress gives nearly identical centerline deformation across Poisson's ratios, while plane strain becomes markedly stiffer at higher Poisson's ratio; hyperelastic models agree closely in global response.
watch_item: Plane-strain reduction can introduce strong Poisson-ratio sensitivity, so the constitutive assumption must be chosen carefully for the intended beam application.
paper_title: On finite elements for geometrically-exact planar beams with hyperelastic material models
